::: {#exm-shares-letter}
#### Words that share a letter

Let $V = \set{\text{cat}, \text{cow}, \text{dog}, \text{pig}}$,
and on $V$ let $a \mathrel{T} b$ when the words $a$ and $b$ have at least one letter in common (@rem-relation-on-set).
For example, $\text{cat} \mathrel{T} \text{cow}$, since both have a c,
and $\text{cow} \mathrel{T} \text{dog}$, since both have an o,
but $(\text{cat}, \text{dog}) \notin T$.
@fig-shares-letter is the directed graph (@def-relation-digraph) of $T$.
Each word has a letter in common with itself,
so each point has an arrow that comes back to it.

::: {#fig-shares-letter}

![](../images/relations-shares-letter.png){fig-alt="A directed graph with points cat, cow, dog and pig in a row, where each point has an arrow back to itself and arrows go both ways between cat and cow, between cow and dog, and between dog and pig." width="70%"}

The directed graph of the relation "shares a letter with" on $V$.
